slides.title: Purpose
bullets: Haemostasis is a biological system that on one hand keeps the blood fluid and on the other prevents bleeding and stops blood loss.
Haemostasis is divided into primary vascular-platelet and secondary coagulation haemostasis.
The system has three components: the vessel wall, the cellular clotting factors (platelets) and the plasma factors.
For a correct result the material must be properly prepared and collected: this protocol gives the collection rules.

slides.title: Preparation and material
bullets: Blood is taken in the morning, fasting.
Compression of the vein for a long time, or much movement of the arm during collection, raises the plasma factors.
The main material for the tests is venous blood in 3.2% sodium citrate.
For aggregation, platelet-rich plasma from blood collected in 3.2% sodium citrate is used.
Capillary blood may be used only for the platelet count, bleeding time, clotting time and rapid diagnosis in newborns.

slides.title: Collection procedure
bullets: 1. Venous stasis (tourniquet) must not last longer than 1 minute.
2. Blood is taken from a vein of the forearm with a wide-bore needle.
3. Blood is drawn into a plastic tube containing 3.2% sodium citrate; a glass tube must not be used.
4. The ratio of blood to 3.2% sodium citrate must be 9:1.

slides.title: Collection procedure
bullets: 5. Deliver the blood to the laboratory promptly; the time allowed from collection to testing depends on the test — follow the laboratory procedure and the reagent instructions.

slides.title: Sources of error
bullets: A tourniquet left on for long, or much arm movement, artificially raises the plasma factors.
A blood-to-citrate ratio other than 9:1 distorts the result.
A glass tube, or a delay beyond the time allowed for the test, makes the material unusable.
Capillary blood is not suitable for all haemostasis tests — only in the cases stated.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: Treat all specimens as potentially containing pathogenic infections; work in rubber gloves.
Needles and sharp objects go into a puncture-proof container.
Wash the hands before drawing blood; wipe the puncture site with 60–90% alcohol from the centre outwards, let it dry and do not palpate it again.
Used materials are disinfected.
